choice: Extend the current handbook and registry roles; resolve logical capability to immutable repository ID, source path, release and consumers.
scope: All first-party components
acceptance: Unique authoritative writer and explicit supersession, no unresolved field silently promoted to fact.
exception_contract: Ambiguous authority blocks only affected writes; useful independent product work continues.

choice: Prefer removal of unnecessary work, existing external/shared capabilities, owned upstream improvement and narrow adapters before new generic implementations.
scope: Libraries, services, tools, docs, patterns and schemas
acceptance: Consumer contract and total ecosystem burden improve; actual installed/imported path uses selected provider.
exception_contract: New implementation is permitted with explicit missing capability and evidence against serious alternatives.

choice: Oxlint is the primary first-party lint engine; map existing semantic rules and enable applicable type-aware coverage.
scope: Eligible JS/TS first-party profiles
acceptance: Seed representative errors for every required rule family; no loss of framework/security/boundary coverage.
exception_contract: A residual rule runner owns named unmatched rules/files only, has an owner, removal trigger and review deadline.

choice: Oxfmt owns supported eligible source formats; route other formats/plugins through explicit disjoint selectors.
scope: JS/TS and supported text formats
acceptance: Determinism, idempotence, semantic preservation and representative plugin/language fixtures.
exception_contract: Unsupported syntax/plugin behavior is an explicit compatibility gap; never run competing formatters on the same file set.

choice: Qualified native TypeScript 7 release, identified by resolved package/version/binary provenance; tsc is a valid native command.
scope: Typecheck/build CLI where supported
acceptance: Every project canary fails independently; diagnostics, module resolution, declarations, build and framework behavior pass.
exception_contract: Keep a scoped compiler-API/framework adapter until replaced with proven parity; do not remove it merely because its name contains typescript.

choice: Pinned Bun with frozen dependency resolution for eligible first-party workspaces.
scope: Install, lockfile and script entry-point ownership
acceptance: Clean-room install, lifecycle-script behavior, workspace resolution, package packing and deploy reproducibility.
exception_contract: Upstream fork install contracts can be retained temporarily with exact boundary and migration proof.

choice: Prefer Bun independently of package-manager choice, after runtime and test-runner conformance.
scope: Owned services, CLIs and tests
acceptance: Production API, native ABI, shutdown, streams, TLS, subprocess, snapshot/mocking and test selection parity.
exception_contract: Node-specific upstream/native behavior must have an owned exception or remediation; no blind executable substitution.

choice: uv owns interpreter/environment/dependency resolution, with frozen locks for application profiles.
scope: Python first-party components
acceptance: Clean environment and explicit interpreter/dependency identities; supported platform matrix.
exception_contract: External binary distribution boundaries may require another tool, never a silently interchangeable environment.

choice: Target CPython 3.14t for eligible owned execution profiles; verify supported build and actual GIL state after relevant imports.
scope: Runtime profiles, not package minimum metadata
acceptance: GIL state, native wheels, race tests, concurrency load and actual time/memory improve or satisfy accepted budgets.
exception_contract: Unsupported extension or unacceptable measured regression is explicit blocked/exception state, not automatic fallback or forced unsafe GIL disable.

choice: Ruff for lint/format; qualify ty as preferred fast type-checker for supported profiles while retaining indispensable scoped API/plugin coverage.
scope: Python owned source
acceptance: Seed missing imports, bad types and framework contracts; intended syntax target matches policy.
exception_contract: Do not silently lose mypy plugin/stub behavior; exact remaining scope is recorded.
authority_status: recommended selection; type-checker promotion requires parity

choice: Lefthook is the single owned hook orchestrator; shared commands also run in mandatory CI.
scope: Active first-party development checkouts
acceptance: Installed hook path, effective config, nested/staged file selection, failure propagation and CI equivalence.
exception_contract: Unmodified upstream checkout can retain its hooks under a fork boundary; do not stack competing managers.

choice: Use maintained FastMCP for Python servers; PhenoFast is a thin shared integration policy layer only where it adds nonduplicated value.
scope: MCP framework, auth/telemetry integration and service bindings
acceptance: Transport/schema/authorization/cancellation/error/shutdown/consumer conformance; no import-success stub counted as service.
exception_contract: Native host profile can use a qualified native SDK when Python adds measurable cost or deployment incompatibility; must implement same external contract.

choice: Reuse actual provider workflows and actions at immutable refs; generate literal consumer wrappers from selected policy release.
scope: GitHub Actions and equivalent local commands
acceptance: Hosted cross-repo call succeeds with correct permissions, dependency pin and exact result provenance.
exception_contract: Private-provider visibility is validated; unavailable provider blocks affected assurance, not substituted echo success.

choice: Separate low-latency, throughput, distribution-size and debug/verification profiles; choose against workload measurements.
scope: Rust/Zig/C++ and equivalent native builds
acceptance: Correctness, sanitizer coverage where applicable, end-to-end benchmarks, symbol/debug policy and build budget.
exception_contract: Hardware-specific artifact must have explicit target dispatch/compatibility; no unsupported instruction surprise.

choice: Broad candidate exploration; production selection is workload-specific and evidence-gated, not popularity- or novelty-gated.
scope: Component or hot path; avoid whole-project rewrite by default
acceptance: Same outputs/tolerances, full boundary overhead, target hardware, consumer install and reproducible net advantage.
exception_contract: A prototype can be admitted without production promotion; no arbitrary requirement that novelty itself lower code quality.

choice: PhenoDocs is a versioned documentation production and federation capability, not a second owner of product meaning.
scope: Shared renderer/search/nav/API-doc pipelines; product-owned content
acceptance: Consumer package install, release-bound references, content/API examples executed, routes/links/versioning and access boundaries validated.
exception_contract: Framework differences use adapters; product content remains near its authority; stale docs are not live specifications.

choice: Consume shared design tokens/components/scenes and a constrained landing composition contract; keep product-specific narrative and interaction.
scope: Web/desktop surfaces and public/internal landings
acceptance: Resolved token origin, no shadow copy, responsive/accessibility/state coverage, interactive and visual review evidence.
exception_contract: A deliberate product visual difference has a named extension seam; shared does not mean identical.

choice: Canonicalize error envelopes, deadlines/cancellation, retry/idempotency, data ownership, cache invalidation and boundary protocols as applicability rules plus tests.
scope: All cross-component behavior
acceptance: Consumer/provider contracts, negative cases and compatibility versions.
exception_contract: Async, remote, event-sourced, cached or durable execution requires its specific need; simple local calls remain valid.

choice: Independent, revision-bound gate inputs; empty/missing/stale/skipped/blocked never pass.
scope: All mandatory quality and adoption checks
acceptance: Negative controls defeat missing tools, wrong revision, zero denominator, swallowed exit and changed evaluator.
exception_contract: Hashes retain identity but do not authenticate a producer or authorize a result.

choice: Every deviation is bounded by subject, capability, rule, reason, alternative proof, owner, expiry and exit condition.
scope: Temporary compatibility or accepted scoped variant
acceptance: Expired/malformed/ambiguous exception fails closed for affected qualification; canonical remains a separate state.
exception_contract: An intentional permanent variant is a first-class profile with its own tests, not an endless temporary waiver.

choice: One writer/lease for shared manifests and releases; bounded parallel component work with independent verification.
scope: Multi-agent development and CI workload scheduling
acceptance: No lost updates, base-ref checks, idempotent retry and explicit cancellation/resource budgets.
exception_contract: Separate unrelated work need not wait on shared governance or a complete atlas.

choice: Consumer-first, reversible migration with exact source mapping; retire old implementation only after actual adoption and provenance preservation.
scope: All shared extraction, tooling migration and repo lifecycle changes
acceptance: Packaging, integration, negative tests, live/installed consumer proof, rollback and license/history retention.
exception_contract: This packet grants no archive/delete/publish/host mutation authority.

choice: Separate non-mutating checks from explicitly invoked repair; permitted cache writes are declared and never conceal source changes.
scope: Lint, typecheck, docs checks, migrations and policy generation
acceptance: Snapshot comparison plus injected known defect fails before repair; generated policy drift detected, not silently fixed.
exception_contract: A named repair task may mutate within its existing authorization.

choice: Record source/version/license/consumer/patch rationale and update trigger; thin upstream-linked deltas instead of anonymous postinstall edits.
scope: External dependencies and internal published packages
acceptance: Clean resolution, scoped patch canaries, license/provenance, advisory response and consumer rollout.
exception_contract: Lockfiles can legitimately resolve version ranges; qualified identity lives in resolved evidence, not manifest spelling alone.
